sense: a written note on a text

terms.gloss: a written comment, a note on a text
evidence: Plin. Ep. 7.20.2: librum meum cum adnotātiōnibus tuīs exspectō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short, under annotātiō, which it would rather spell adn-: “a noting down in writing, a remark, annotation (post-Aug.)”.

terms.gloss: comment on, mark (points in a text)
evidence: Plin. Ep. 7.20.1: adnotāvī quae commūtanda, quae eximenda arbitrārer
terms.comment: What Pliny and Tacitus did with each other’s books, and what a reviewer does to a draft or to code. Post-Augustan, like the noun.

phrases.latin: Librum tuum lēgī et, quam dīligentissimē potuī, adnotāvī quae commūtanda, quae eximenda arbitrārer. … Nunc ā tē librum meum cum adnotātiōnibus tuīs exspectō.
phrases.english: I’ve read your book and, as carefully as I could, marked what I thought should be changed and what cut. … Now I’m waiting for my own book back from you, with your comments.

sources: Lewis & Short: annotatio · Lewis & Short: annoto
